proposals.evidence: DEDR3684 gives Kolami nīv thou (oblique in-), alongside Naiki nīv and Telugu nīvu. LSI niva Thou differs in first-vowel quantity and final a, but the singular second-person form fits this family. The separate LSI You record is held because its number is uncertain.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1 explicitly includes Kolami ad in the remote-demonstrative paradigm, specifically woman/thing; the masculine form is am/amd. LSI ad He is therefore proposed at the whole demonstrative article, with its masculine English gloss explicitly unresolved and unchanged. This is family identification, not confirmation of the source gender gloss.
